To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
both CMM and basal cell carcinoma are related to sun exposure.

1) sun exposure during beach holiday is associated with both CMM and basal cell carcinoma; 2) this association is stronger for CMM than for basal cell carcinoma; and 3) the risk of CMM and basal-cell carcinoma increases with the cumulation of sun exposure during holidays.

the risk of CMM is strongly associated with skin phenotype and tendency to sunburn and is increased by intermittent sun exposure, while risk of BCC is associated with skin phenotype, tendency to sun burn and cumulative hours of sun exposure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model for the prediction of the risk of melanoma and nonmelanoma skin cancers based on the analysis of sun exposure and other risk factors.

the development of a parallel risk assessment model for the two main cutaneous cancers, which is based on the evaluation of the strength of the risk association of constitutional factors (tendency to sunburn and skin phenotype) and sun exposure (cumulated sun exposure in childhood and sun exposure during beach vacations) with CMM and B CC.
the development of a new method of assessing risk in the context of a case-control study.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the risk of both types of skin tumours increases with increasing tendency to sunburn, with intermittent sun exposure, with increasing number of hours of sun exposure in a lifetime and with fair skin.
the risk of both types of tumour was associated with the tendency to sunburn and with sun exposure during beach vacations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the most important risk indicators for both tumours are the same, but the effect of risk factors is not identical, and that the risk of CMM and BCD increases with sun exposure, but at different levels.
sunburns in early life are important for melanoma and sunburns in adult life are important for basal cell carcinoma.
melanoma risk is strongly influenced by sun exposure and skin phenotype, whereas basal cell carcinoma is mainly influenced by sun exposure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sunburn and cumulative exposure are important risk factors for both types of skin cancer.

the risk of both types of tumour is strongly associated with the same risk factors, but that the risk of CMM is higher in subjects with fair skin, while the risk of BCC is higher in subjects who tan easily.
there are some differences between the two types of skin cancer, and that there is a need for more research to understand the differences.
